extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of history/political theory interested in US foreign policy and territorial expansion
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter excerpt analyzing the principles, causes, and administrative practices relating to United States territorial expansion and the handling of newly acquired transmarine dominions around 1898–1910. Discusses national temperament, strategic motives, and practical governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: National pacific temperament / aversion to conquest
rubrics_metrics.description: They are, and have usually been, pacific in their views... They have no lust of conquest. They have always been extremely jealous of a standing army... the true way for the model Republic to influence that world is to avoid its errors, and set an example of pacific industrialism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the unjustifiable war with Mexico was the work of the slave‑holding oligarchy and opposed to the general sentiment of the people. Consequence: a very small army sufficed; army officers occupied in scientific/engineering work rather than politics; general national preference for avoiding foreign entanglements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of Old World engagements / neutrality and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute neutrality and impartiality as regards the Old World is observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration: the United States declined to ratify the International Act of the Berlin Conference of 1885 regulating the Congo Free State, and only after delay ratified the Brussels International Slave Trade Act (1892). The public sentiment inclines to abstain from engagements affecting the Old World.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monroe Doctrine / prevent European controlling influence in the New World
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration of a purpose to prevent any European power from attempting to obtain a controlling influence in New World affairs (Monroe's Message of 1823).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: assertion of this principle is less needed as US strength grows, but it remains the complement to the US tendency toward abstinence from Old World affairs; occasions to apply it are comparatively few and unlikely to involve grave difficulties with European powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peaceful acquisition: purchase or voluntary union; natural contiguous expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: All this added territory... came peaceably by way of purchase or (in the case of Texas) voluntary union; the limits of what may be called natural expansion have now been reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: expansion should be by peaceful means and consist of regions which naturally cohere with the original Republic. Exceptions (e.g., Alaska) noted; desire for annexation not stronger than before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexation only as admission as State or Territory; US unsuited to rule dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The only form annexation can with advantage take is the admission of the annexed district as a self‑governing State or Territory... Administrative system singularly unfitted for the rule of dependencies, because it has no proper machinery for controlling provincial governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risks of creating dependencies include jobbing of administrative posts, maladministration, and political corruption. Territories were often given near-complete self-government; dependent countries might be maladministered by appointive officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider demographic, linguistic, and political fitness before annexation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Indo‑Spaniards of Mexico have not as yet shown much fitness for the exercise of political power... inhabitants speaking Spanish only, and containing a negro element... with low literacy (Puerto Rico example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical concerns: admitting populations with different race/language/culture and low literacy to Federal suffrage might injure Federal politics, demoralize officials, supply fertile soil for roguery, and bring jobs/jobbers to Washington. Hence readiness for self-government and compatibility with US institutions are evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic acquisitions as naval stations vs. colonization
rubrics_metrics.description: Guam and Tutuila are nothing more than naval coaling stations... the position of [Hawaii] over against their own Western coast would be so threatening to their commerce in a war ... that they could not suffer the islands to be occupied by, or even to fall under the influence of, any European nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisitions may be justified on strategic grounds (naval bases, coaling stations) rather than as candidates for eventual statehood or assimilation. Hawaii was annexed partly to secure a naval station (Pearl Harbour/Peal River).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt governance to local conditions for transmarine dominions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of these five acquisitions has been dealt with in a separate and distinct way. Hawaii erected into a Territory with governor and legislature; Puerto Rico given a colonial organization with a partly elected lower house and appointed upper house; Philippines given municipal councils, sanitary reforms, and native appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration measures include constructing roads, sanitary reforms, setting up municipal councils elected by the people, appointing natives to administrative posts, settling friars on liberal terms, forbidding Chinese immigration, and restricting land uptake by incorporated companies. The form of government should reflect local population composition and practical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid militarism; caution about increasing armaments
rubrics_metrics.description: The possession of powerful armaments is apt to inspire a wish to use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason for limited standing forces: small army sufficient for internal frontier duties; expansion of navy sometimes criticized in Europe; US ability to protect citizens measured by vast resources rather than number of vessels. Excess armament risks encouraging aggressive policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic push for expansion: capital and population pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: When capital... is no longer able to find highly profitable employment in the development of Western North America, it will tend to seek other fields... When population has filled up the present territory... enterprising spirits will overflow into undeveloped regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predictive principle: economic and demographic pressures make Western South America and other undeveloped regions likely targets for closer US relations or investment, not necessarily formal annexation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendliness with Britain reduces appetite for annexation of Canada
rubrics_metrics.description: There is reason to think that even if Canada were separated from the British Empire, the Americans would not be eager to bring her into the Union... one reason is the growing friendliness of the Americans to Britain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors supporting this: settlement of the Alabama claims, democratization of Britain, growth of literature and science in America, and increased mutual respect and ease of travel (ocean steamers) promoting knowledge between peoples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for independent development of neighbouring polities
rubrics_metrics.description: It is more to the advantage, both of the United States and of the Canadians, that they should continue to develop independent types of political life and intellectual progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative guidance: each polity, by working out its own institutions, may have something to teach the other; excessive political union would reduce variety on the continent.
